results.summary: This project implements a multiplication and accumulation (MAC) operation in Verilog. It takes two 8-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit output, likely the accumulated result. The documentation is minimal, stating only that it multiplies and accumulates data, and suggests testing with a memory operation. No external hardware is specified, and the design's exact behavior and interface are not fully described.

TinyQV is a small RISC-V SoC implementing the RV32EC instruction set with Zcb and Zicond extensions, using QSPI flash for program storage and QSPI PSRAM for data memory. It includes a UART and SPI controller, and is intended to be used with a QSPI PMOD containing flash and RAM, as well as an ST7789 LCD display and game controller. The QSPI clock and data lines are shared between the flash and the RAM, so only one can be accessed simultaneously. Data can be read from flash and RAM, and written to RAM.

This project implements a simple XOR cipher with UART communication. It uses a UART interface for data input and output, and the cipher operation is performed on the received data. The design is purely digital and requires no external hardware. The exact key handling and encryption details are not fully described.

This project is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit inputs to produce an 8-bit product. It is built using structural Verilog and consists of AND gates and full adders arranged in an array. Testing can be done by applying input values and observing the output product. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware.

The result is output on an 8-bit output bus, which can be connected to an external display or register. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware.

The design has four internal registers that can be read and written via SPI. The exact floating-point format and rounding behavior are not described.
